chunks: As it is narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)

(that he said: "If only one day were to remain from the tenure of the world, Allah would prolong that day until a man from my progeny emerges, and he would fill the earth with justice and equity, just as it was filled with injustice and oppression.")
ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet say about the duration of the world and the emergence of justice?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from Al-Ghayba highlights the eschatological role of the Mahdi (a.s.) as the restorer of divine justice, a concept central to Shia belief in the eventual global dominion of Islam. The mention of Allah extending a single day underscores the certainty of the event, regardless of the duration of the occultation, while the contrast between 'zulm' (oppression) and 'adl' (justice) reflects the cosmic balance sought in the end times. This narrative is often cited to reassure believers during the long occultation that the ultimate triumph of the Ahl al-Bayt is divinely guaranteed.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: “Even if only a day remains from the tenure of the world, Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, would prolong it enough to allow a man from my progeny to appear. Then he would fill up the earth with justice and equity just as it would be fraught with injustice and oppression.”
